record.title: Kriesell's spanning-tree deletion conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. A graph is **$r$-connected** if it remains connected after deletion of fewer than $r$ vertices. For a spanning tree $T$ of a graph $G$, write $G-E(T)$ for the graph obtained by deleting all edges of $T$.

**Kriesell's conjecture.** There exists a smallest integer $g(k)$ such that every $g(k)$-connected graph $G$ contains a spanning tree $T$ for which

$$
G-E(T)\text{ is }k\text{-connected}.
$$

The paper's packing theorem implies this conjecture, with an explicit bound obtained from the paper's results. Earlier work established the case $k=2$, while the edge-connected analogue follows from the Nash-Williams–Tutte theorem.
record.source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi, Tibor Jordán, Csaba Király and Soma Villányi, “Highly connected orientations from edge-disjoint rigid subgraphs”, arXiv:2401.12670 (2025).
record.references:
**8 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2209.06204](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06204), [arXiv:2206.12092](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12092), [arXiv:2110.12783](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.12783), [arXiv:2110.13726](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.13726), [arXiv:1207.1838](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.1838), [arXiv:1201.3727](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.3727), [arXiv:1112.0127](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.0127).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12670

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Conditional lower-bound conjecture for mixed cages
record.statement:
Let $n[z,r;g]$ be the minimum order of a $[z,r;g]$-mixed cage, and let $n_{\operatorname{AHM}}[1,r;g]$ denote the AHM bound appearing in the source. **Conditional lower-bound conjecture.** If the conjecture that $n[z,g]=z(g-1)+1$ is true, then

$$
n[z,r;g]\geq z(g-1)+1+n_{\operatorname{AHM}}[1,r;g]-g.
$$

This is an immediate conditional consequence of the stated lower bound $n[z,r;g]\geq n[z,g]+n_{\operatorname{AHM}}[1,r;g]-g$; the source does not establish the antecedent conjecture or resolve the resulting bound.
record.source_name: Gabriela Araujo-Pardo and Mirabel Mendoza-Cadena, “On Mixed Cages of Girth 6”, arXiv:2401.14768 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.14768

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

record.title: Diameter conjecture for large subsets of classical compact groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be one of $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $\mathrm{SO}(n)$, $\mathrm{Spin}(n)$, or $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, and let $\mathcal{A}\subseteq G$ be measurable with measure $
u$. The diameter with respect to $\mathcal{A}$ is the smallest positive integer $t$ such that $\mathcal{A}^t=G$. **Diameter conjecture.** The diameter of $G$ with respect to $\mathcal{A}$ is $O(
u^{-1/(\ell n)})$, where $\ell=1$ for $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ and $\mathrm{Spin}(n)$, $\ell=2$ for $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, and $\ell=4$ for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$. In particular, if $
u\geqslant e^{-cn}$, then the diameter is at most $O_c(1)$. This concerns uniform diameter bounds for large measurable subsets of the classical compact groups; the excerpt gives no resolution.
record.source_name: David Ellis, Guy Kindler, Noam Lifshitz and Dor Minzer, “Product Mixing in Compact Lie Groups”, arXiv:2401.15456 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15456

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2024).

record.title: Existence of a knot with distinct minimum and maximum thin-position heights
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot. For a thin position $\gamma$ of $K$, let $ht(\gamma)$ be the number of thick level spheres, and define $ht(K)$ and $ht_{\min}(K)$ to be the maximum and minimum, respectively, of $ht(\gamma)$ over all thin positions of $K$.

**Height variation conjecture.** There is a knot $K$ such that

$$
ht_{\min}(K)<ht(K).
$$

This conjecture asks whether a knot can have thin positions with different numbers of thick level spheres. The source provides no resolution, so the problem remains open.
record.source_name: Ricky Lee, Puttipong Pongtanapaisan and Hanh Vo, “Widths of links via diagram colorings”, arXiv:2401.17193 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.17193

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

record.title: Noble-number conjecture for the local minima of the Brjuno function
record.statement:
Let $B_1$ denote the classical Brjuno function, let $
\mathcal{M}$ be the set of its local minima, and let $\mathcal{N}$ be the set of noble numbers, namely the numbers whose regular continued fraction expansion is of the form $[0;a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n,\overline{1}]$. **Local-minima conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{N}.
$$

The global minimum of $B_1$ is known to be attained at the golden number, and the cited corollary gives the corresponding lower bound on $(0,1/2)$. Numerical evidence suggests that all local minima, not only these known global-minimum examples, are precisely the noble numbers.
record.source_name: Ayreena Bakhtawar, Carlo Carminati and Stefano Marmi, “Global and local minima of α-Brjuno functions”, arXiv:2401.17679 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.17679

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

record.title: The doubled-prefix conjecture for reduced banned words
record.statement:
Let $1/2<\rho<1$ be a scaling factor, and let $\{\alpha^i\}_{i\in I}$ be the reduced banned words, enumerated in nondecreasing order of length, with $I\subseteq\mathbb{N}$. For each $i\in I$, write

$$
\gamma^i=\alpha^i|_{[1,|\alpha^i|-1]}.
$$

A **doubled-prefix conjecture** asserts that, for every $i\in I$, the concatenation $\gamma^i\gamma^i$ does not contain any $\alpha^j$ with $j\leq i$ as a subword.

This condition is intended to support the observed recursive pattern in the reduced banned words and the converse of the sufficient condition for an iterated function system to be of finite type. The source says that proving the assertion or finding a counterexample is very difficult; the supplied status evidence marks it as disproved, although no explicit counterexample is provided here.
record.source_name: Grover Lancaster-Cole, Georgiana Lyall, Thomas Malcolm and Qiyu Zhou, “Graph Iterated Function Systems and Fractal Tops”, arXiv:2402.00237 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.00237

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2024). “It turns out to be very difficult to prove or find a counterexample.”

record.title: Optimality conjecture for the 2-neighborly-box construction
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ be the non-decreasing list of all positive integers except $1$, with each number $3\cdot2^r$ repeated twice, and define

$$
b(d)=4+a(1)+\cdots+a(d-2)\quad(d\geqslant3),\qquad b(2)=4.
$$

Let $n(2,d)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise $2$-neighborly boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. **Optimality conjecture.** For each $d\geqslant2$, $n(2,d)=b(d)$. The paper's construction proves the lower bound $n(2,d)\geqslant b(d)$, so the conjecture asks for the matching upper bound.
record.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Andrzej P. Kisielewicz and Krzysztof Przesławski, “Neighborly boxes and bipartite coverings; constructions and conjectures”, arXiv:2402.02199 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02199

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “This supposition is supported by some numerical experiments and some partial results on related open problems which are recalled.”

record.title: Parity-sensitive representation conjecture for nonnormal cycle-generated Cayley graphs
record.statement: Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, and for $1\leq r<k\leq n-2$ let $C(n,k;r)$ be the set of $k$-cycles moving every point from $1$ to $r$. Write $\rho_{(n-1,1)}$ for the standard representation and $\rho_{(2,1^{n-2})}$ for its sign twist. The **parity-sensitive representation conjecture.** For $n\geq 5$, if $k$ is even, the second largest eigenvalue of $\operatorname{Cay}(S_n,C(n,k;r))$ is attained uniquely by $\rho_{(n-1,1)}$; if $k$ is odd, the strictly second largest eigenvalue is attained exactly by $\rho_{(n-1,1)}$ and $\rho_{(2,1^{n-2})}$. The conjecture is presented as stronger than the preceding partial theorems, and no resolution is supplied in the source excerpt.
record.source_name: Yuxuan Li, Binzhou Xia and Sanming Zhou, “The second largest eigenvalue of some nonnormal Cayley graphs on symmetric groups”, arXiv:2402.02427 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02427

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2024). “Recently, this conjecture was fully proved in , where the authors of the present paper discussed the strictly second largest eigenvalue of $\mathrm{Cay}(S_n,C(n,I))$ with $C(n,I)=\cup_{k\in I} C(n,k)$ and $I\subseteq \{2,3,\ldots,n\}$.”

record.title: The non-principal pair of posets conjecture for the incidence graph of $K_4$
record.statement:
Let $G_4=(A,B,E)$ be the bipartite incidence graph of the complete graph $K_4$, with $A=E(K_4)$, $B=V(K_4)$, and $(e,v)\in E$ exactly when $v\in e$. Let $P_{G_4,A}$ and $P_{G_4,B}$ be the associated posets, and let $\mathop{}\!\mathrm{La}(n,\{P_{G_4,A},P_{G_4,B}\})$ denote the maximum size of a family in $2^{[n]}$ containing neither poset. **The non-principal pair of posets conjecture.**

$$
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{La}(n,P_{G_4,A})-\mathop{}\!\mathrm{La}(n,\{P_{G_4,A},P_{G_4,B}\})=\Omega\left(\binom{n}{n/2}\right).
$$

This predicts that the family of posets $\{P_{G_4,A},P_{G_4,B}\}$ is not asymptotically principal: forbidding both posets costs a positive-order middle-layer term beyond forbidding $P_{G_4,A}$ alone. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner and Balázs Patkós, “A note on vertex Turán problems in the Kneser cube”, arXiv:2402.02525 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02525

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Multipartite Hajnal–Szemerédi perfect packing conjecture
record.statement: Let $k\ge 2$ and let $G$ be a $k$-partite graph with parts $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ of the same size $n$. Define the **partite minimum degree** of $G$ to be the largest integer $d$ such that every vertex has at least $d$ neighbors in each part other than its own. A **perfect $K_k$-packing** is a collection of vertex-disjoint $k$-cliques covering all vertices of $G$. **Fischer–Kühn–Osthus's conjecture.** If the partite minimum degree of $G$ is at least $\left(1-\frac{1}{k}\right)n$, then $G$ has a perfect $K_k$-packing unless both $k$ and $n$ are odd and $G$ is isomorphic to a single exceptional graph. The statement is presented as an application conjecture in the source; its resolution status is not given.
record.source_name: Debsoumya Chakraborti and Tuan Tran, “Approximate packing of independent transversals in locally sparse graphs”, arXiv:2402.02815 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02815

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Kuperwasser–Samotij–Wigderson forest-removal conjecture
record.statement:
Let $m>0$ be a real number. For a graph $G$, write $m(G)$ for its maximum average density and $m_2(G)$ for its 2-density. **Kuperwasser–Samotij–Wigderson conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $m(G)\leq m$ contains a forest $F\subseteq G$ such that

$$
m_2(G-F)\leq m.
$$

The conjecture strengthens a known result in which $F$ is only required to be a pseudoforest. The supplied source does not state that this conjecture itself has been proved; the cited implication concerns a further generalization, so its database status remains open.
record.source_name: Micha Christoph, Anders Martinsson, Raphael Steiner and Yuval Wigderson, “Resolution of the Kohayakawa-Kreuter conjecture”, arXiv:2402.03045 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03045

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2024). “Namely, as proved in , would imply a natural generalization of where one wishes to color $G_{n,p}$ and avoid not just a single graph $H_i$ in color $i$, but some finite family $\{H_i^{(1)},\dots,H_i^{(t)}\}$.”

record.title: An FPRAS for counting list packings
record.statement: Let $\Delta$ be a maximum-degree bound, let $q\ge 2\Delta$, and consider graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$. A $q$-list packing assigns colors from each vertex's list so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint color sets. **Counting conjecture.** For each $\Delta$ and $q\ge 2\Delta$, there is a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme (FPRAS) for counting the number of $q$-list packings of graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$. This would give an efficient approximate-counting algorithm throughout the stated range, extending the algorithmic study of list packing; the source does not indicate that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Evan Camrud, Ewan Davies, Alex Karduna and Holden Lee, “Sampling List Packings”, arXiv:2402.03520 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03520

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Grünbaum's conjecture on spanning trees and co-trees of planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar 3-connected graph. A **3-tree** is a spanning tree of $G$ with maximum degree at most $3$. For a spanning tree $T$ of $G$, let $G^*=(V^*,E^*)$ be the planar dual and define its **co-tree** by

$$
\neg T^*:= (V^*,(E(G)-E(T))^*).
$$

**Grünbaum's conjecture.** Every planar 3-connected graph $G$ contains a 3-tree $T$ whose co-tree $\neg T^*$ is also a 3-tree.

The conjecture strengthens the separate existence of bounded-degree spanning trees by requiring the spanning tree and its dual co-tree simultaneously to have maximum degree at most $3$. It remains open; Biedl proved the weaker bound that there is a spanning tree such that both it and its co-tree have maximum degree at most $5$.
record.source_name: Christian Ortlieb and Jens M. Schmidt, “Toward Grünbaum's Conjecture”, arXiv:2402.05681 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1312.4101](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.4101).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05681

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “While Grünbaum's conjecture remains open, Biedl proved that there is a spanning tree $T$ such that $T$ and its co-tree have maximum degree at most 5.”

record.title: The resistance and edge-reduction conjecture for snarks
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a snark. Define the **resistance** $r(G)$ to be the minimum number of edges that can be removed from $G$ so that the resulting graph is $3$-edge-colorable, and define $e_r(G)$ to be the minimum number of pairwise non-adjacent edges whose removal and subsequent suppression of incident vertices produces a $3$-edge-colorable graph. **Resistance and edge-reduction conjecture.**

$$
r(G)\geq 2e_r(G).
$$

This conjectured relation connects two measures of how far a snark is from being $3$-edge-colorable and is stated as a conjecture in the cited literature; no resolution is supplied in the paper.
record.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Proper Z4 x Z2-colorings: structural characterization with application to some snarks”, arXiv:2402.06008 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06008

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: The equivariant DT–PT₀ correspondence
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a Calabi–Yau 4-fold with an algebraic torus $T$ acting while preserving the Calabi–Yau volume form, and let $L$ be a $T$-equivariant line bundle on $X$. For $\gamma\in H_c^4(X,\mathbb Q)$ and $\beta\in H_c^6(X,\mathbb Q)$, suppose that $\curly P_{\gamma,\beta,n}^{(q)}(X)^T$ consists of isolated reduced points for every $n$ and $q\in\{-1,0\}$. **Equivariant DT–PT₀ correspondence.** There are choices of square roots at all $T$-fixed points such that

$$
\frac{\sum_n\langle\!\langle L\rangle\!\rangle_{X,\gamma,\beta,n}^{\mathrm{DT}}q^n}{\sum_n\langle\!\langle L\rangle\!\rangle_{X,0,0,n}^{\mathrm{DT}}q^n}=\sum_n\langle\!\langle L\rangle\!\rangle_{X,\gamma,\beta,n}^{\mathrm{PT}_0}q^n
$$

as an identity of Laurent series in $q$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(t^{1/2},y^{1/2})$. This is the equivariant refinement of the DT–PT₀ correspondence under isolated-reduced-fixed-point hypotheses; no general resolution is stated.
record.source_name: Younghan Bae, Martijn Kool and Hyeonjun Park, “Counting surfaces on Calabi-Yau 4-folds II: DT-PT_0 correspondence”, arXiv:2402.06526 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06526

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2024). “Its numerical version was proved combinatorially in and its full $K$-theoretic version was recently established in .”

record.title: Genus bound for reconstructing non-separable matroids from Tutte polynomials
record.statement: Let $M$ be a non-separable matroid. Let $C$ be a largest circuit of $M$, let $D$ be a largest cocircuit of $M$, and let $\mathcal{B}(M)$ denote the set appearing in the genus bound. **Genus reconstruction conjecture.** Then $M$ can be reconstructed from its Tutte polynomial of genus $|\mathcal{B}(M)|-\max\{|C|,|D|\}+3$. The paper presents this as an open problem that the authors believe can be proved, extending the policy used in the proof of the main theorem.
record.source_name: Tsuyoshi Miezaki, Manabu Oura, Tadashi Sakuma and Hidehiro Shinohara, “The Tutte polynomials of genus g”, arXiv:2402.06845 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06845

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: The weighted projective Serre bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $a_0,ots,a_n$ be positive weights, and let $e_q(d;a_0,a_1,ots,a_n)$ be the maximum number of ${\mathbb F}_q$-rational points on a hypersurface of weighted degree $d$ in ${\mathbb P}(a_0,ots,a_n)$. Let $p_n=q^n+ots+q+1$ for $n\geq 0$ and $p_n=0$ for $n<0$. **The weighted projective Serre bound conjecture.** If $a_0=1$, $\operatorname{lcm}(a_1,a_2,ots,a_n)\mid d$, and $a_1\leq a_2\leqots\leq a_n$, then

$$
e_q(d;1,a_1,a_2,ots,a_n)=\min\left\{p_n,\frac{d}{a_1}q^{n-1}+p_{n-2}\right\}.
$$

The conjecture generalizes the Serre bound from ordinary projective spaces to weighted projective spaces. The paper proves it in every dimension when the second weight is also one, so the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Yves Aubry and Marc Perret, “Maximum number of rational points on hypersurfaces in weighted projective spaces over finite fields”, arXiv:2402.07522 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07522

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Gorodnik–Varjú's super approximation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$. Write $\mathbb{G}$ for the Zariski closure of $G$, and let $\mathbb{G}_0$ be its identity component. The group $G$ has the **super approximation property** with respect to all positive integers if there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that the Cheeger constants of the Cayley graphs of the reductions of $G$ are greater than $\epsilon$ for every positive integer modulus. **Gorodnik–Varjú's super approximation conjecture.** The group $G$ has the super approximation property with respect to all positive integers if and only if $\mathbb{G}_0$ is perfect, that is, 
$$
[\mathbb{G}_0,\mathbb{G}_0]=\mathbb{G}_0.
$$
 This conjecture characterizes uniform expansion over all congruence quotients in terms of the algebraic structure of the identity component of the Zariski closure. The source attributes it to Gorodnik and Varjú; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Chong Zhang, “The super approximation property of SL_2(Z/qZ) SL_2(Z/qZ) SL_2(Z/qZ)”, arXiv:2402.08612 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08612

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Li–Li edge-connection conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-edge-connected graph, where $k\ge 2$, and let $H\subset G$ be a **minimum-edge spanning $k$-edge-connected subgraph**, meaning a spanning $k$-edge-connected subgraph with minimum $e(H)$. **Li–Li edge-connection conjecture.**

$$
emc_k(G)=e(G)-e(H)+\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is presented as the edge-connectivity analogue of the paper's monochromatic $k$-connection conjecture.
record.source_name: Qingqiong Cai, Shinya Fujita, Henry Liu and Boram Park, “Monochromatic k-connection of graphs”, arXiv:2402.09254 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09254

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Bipartite monochromatic $k$-connection conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-connected bipartite graph with partition classes of sizes $s$ and $t$, where $t\ge s\ge k\ge 2$, and let $H\subset G$ be a minimum spanning $k$-connected subgraph. **Bipartite monochromatic $k$-connection conjecture.** If

$$
e(H)=kt,
$$

then

$$
mc_k(G)=e(G)-kt+h_k(G).
$$

For such bipartite graphs, $kt$ is the relevant minimum possible edge count for a spanning $k$-connected subgraph, so this specializes the general conjecture to the bipartite setting.
record.source_name: Qingqiong Cai, Shinya Fujita, Henry Liu and Boram Park, “Monochromatic k-connection of graphs”, arXiv:2402.09254 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09254

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Complete bipartite graph monochromatic $k$-connection conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $s$ and $t$. **Complete bipartite monochromatic $k$-connection conjecture.** For $t\ge s\ge k\ge 2$,

$$
mc_k(K_{s,t})=st-kt+h_k(K_{s,t}),
$$

and, for $t\ge k\ge 2$,

$$
mc_k(K_{t,t})=t^2-kt+1.
$$

The first assertion specializes the bipartite conjecture to complete bipartite graphs; the second uses that a minimum spanning $k$-connected subgraph of $K_{t,t}$ has $kt$ edges and that its corresponding $h_k$ value is $1$.
record.source_name: Qingqiong Cai, Shinya Fujita, Henry Liu and Boram Park, “Monochromatic k-connection of graphs”, arXiv:2402.09254 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09254

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Constant-additive coloring conjecture for pseudoline arrangements
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of pseudolines, and let $\operatorname{mx}(\mathcal{A})$ denote the maximum number of crossings on any pseudoline. A coloring of the crossings is proper along pseudolines if no color appears twice along any pseudoline. **Constant-additive coloring conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ so that the crossings of every pseudoline arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ can be colored using $\operatorname{mx}(\mathcal{A})+c$ colors so that no color appears twice along any pseudoline. This asks whether the chromatic requirement for arrangements of pseudolines differs from the maximum number of crossings on one pseudoline by at most an absolute additive constant.
record.source_name: Sandro Roch, “Coloring problems on arrangements of pseudolines”, arXiv:2402.12564 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12564

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Lawson surfaces minimize area among minimal surfaces of fixed genus
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}_\gamma$ be the minimum area among all minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{S}^3$ of genus $\gamma$, and let $\xi_{\gamma,1}$ be the Lawson surface of genus $\gamma$. **Lawson area-minimization conjecture.** The minimum area $\mathcal{A}_\gamma$ is uniquely attained by $\xi_{\gamma,1}$. This is presented as a special case of a conjecture characterizing Lawson surfaces as Willmore minimizers.
record.source_name: Mikhail Karpukhin, Robert Kusner, Peter McGrath and Daniel Stern, “Embedded minimal surfaces in S^3 and B^3 via equivariant eigenvalue optimization”, arXiv:2402.13121 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13121

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2024). “The fact that $\mathrm{ind}(\xi_{\gamma, 1}) = 2\gamma+3$ was established by Kapouleas-Wiygul .”

record.title: The generating-ideal conjecture for weak polynomial identities of the Weyl algebra
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field of characteristic zero. The Weyl algebra $\mathsf{A}_1$ is generated by $x,y$ with relation $yx=xy+1$, and let $\mathsf{V}=\mathbb{F}\text{-}\operatorname{span}\{x,y\}$. Let $\mathbb{F}\langle X\rangle$ be the free associative algebra, and let $\mathcal{I}$ be the L-ideal generated by

$$
\Gamma_3(x_i,x_j,x_k),\qquad {\rm St}_3(x_i,x_j,x_k),\qquad T_4(x_i,x_j,x_k,x_l)
$$

for all positive indices. A weak polynomial identity for $(\mathsf{A}_1,\mathsf{V})$ is an element of $\mathbb{F}\langle X\rangle$ vanishing under substitutions from $\mathsf{V}$ into $\mathsf{A}_1$.

**Generating-ideal conjecture.** The ideal of all weak polynomial identities for the pair $(\mathsf{A}_1,\mathsf{V})$ is equal to $\mathcal{I}$.

The paper establishes the claim for two variables and for degrees four and five, while the conjecture concerns weak polynomial identities in all numbers of variables and degrees.
record.source_name: Artem Lopatin, Carlos Arturo Rodriguez Palma and Liming Tang, “Weak polynomial identities of small degree for the Weyl algebra”, arXiv:2402.14799 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14799

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Equivalent maximal-ReLU-function minimal-depth conjecture
record.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be the coordinate functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let the minimal depth of a CPWL function mean the smallest $m$ for which it is representable by a ReLU neural network in $\Upsilon(m)$.

**Hertrich et al.'s equivalent conjecture.** The function

$$
\max\{x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,0\}
$$

has minimal depth $\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$.

The paper states this as an equivalent formulation of the general minimum-depth conjecture. It is known in dimensions $n=2,3$, while the general assertion remains open.

record.title: The $(S_2)$-condition conjecture for edge rings of triangular cactus graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a **triangular cactus graph**, meaning a cactus graph whose blocks are all $3$-cycles, and let its diameter be the maximum distance between two vertices of $G$. The **$(S_2)$-condition conjecture.** The edge ring associated to a triangular cactus graph of diameter at least $4$ satisfies Serre's condition $(S_2)$. This conjecture extends the known cases of triangular cactus graphs of diameter at most $3$, whose edge rings are normal and Cohen--Macaulay; the paper proves the claim for triangular cactus graphs of diameter $4$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Rodica Dinu and Nayana Shibu Deepthi, “On the (S_2)-condition of edge rings for cactus graphs”, arXiv:2402.17413 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17413

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Absorber degeneracy conjecture for cliques
record.statement:
For a fixed graph $L$, let $d_{\rm abs}(L)$ denote the absorber degeneracy parameter used in the source. Here $K_q$ denotes the complete graph on $q$ vertices.

**Absorber degeneracy conjecture.** For each integer $q\geq 3$,

$$
d_{\rm abs}(K_q)=q.
$$

The preceding argument establishes only the lower bound $d_{\rm abs}(K_q)\geq q-1$. Thus the conjecture proposes the exact value and remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Michelle Delcourt, Tom Kelly and Luke Postle, “Clique Decompositions in Random Graphs via Refined Absorption”, arXiv:2402.17857 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17857

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2024). “This conjecture was settled by the combined work of several sets of authors .”

record.title: Gastineau–Togni and Hocquard–Lajou–Lužar conjecture on $(1,2^7)$-edge-coloring
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, a **$(1,2^7)$-edge-coloring** partitions $E(G)$ into one matching and seven induced matchings. A graph is **subcubic** if its maximum degree is at most $3$.

**The $(1,2^7)$-edge-coloring conjecture.** Every subcubic graph is $(1,2^7)$-edge-colorable.

Gastineau and Togni first asked this as an open question for cubic graphs, while Hocquard, Lajou, and Lužar conjectured the stated subcubic version. The paper reports it as unresolved; known results establish the weaker $(1,2^8)$-edge-coloring bound.
record.source_name: Xujun Liu and Gexin Yu, “On the (1^2,2^4)-packing edge-coloring of subcubic graphs”, arXiv:2402.18353 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18353

record.title: Maximum-likelihood degree formula for generic polygon Wachspress models
record.statement:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{(n-2) \times n}_{\geq 0}$ be generic among matrices having a cell whose fibers are $n$-gons. Let $C \subset C_{\max}$ be a cell, choose $b \in \operatorname{int}(C)$, let $P_b$ be the corresponding fiber, and set $Q=B^T \cdot P_b$. Denote by $M_{\mathbb{C}}(Q)$ the Wachspress model of $Q$.

**Wachspress ML-degree conjecture.** For a generic $n$-gon $Q$, the maximum likelihood degree is

$$
\operatorname{MLdeg}(M_{\mathbb{C}}(Q))=(n-1)(n-2)+(n-3)(n-5)-1.
$$

The conjecture gives the predicted maximum likelihood degree for generic polygonal Wachspress models. The paper presents it as an expected formula and does not establish it unconditionally.
record.source_name: Dmitrii Pavlov and Simon Telen, “Santaló Geometry of Convex Polytopes”, arXiv:2402.18955 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18955

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Non-degeneracy conjecture for adjoints of generic polygonal Wachspress models
record.statement:
Let $Q=B^T\cdot P_b$ be a generic $n$-gon, and let $\alpha_Q$ denote its adjoint polynomial. A Laurent polynomial is **non-degenerate** with respect to its Newton polytope when its face polynomials define smooth hypersurfaces in the corresponding algebraic tori.

**Adjoint non-degeneracy conjecture.** For a generic $n$-gon $Q=B^T\cdot P_b$, the adjoint $\alpha_Q$ is non-degenerate, with Newton polytope equal to the Newton polytope of

$$
(1+y_1+y_2)^{n-3}.
$$

This conjecture is the geometric input for the predicted maximum-likelihood-degree formula of the Wachspress model. The source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Dmitrii Pavlov and Simon Telen, “Santaló Geometry of Convex Polytopes”, arXiv:2402.18955 (2024).

record.title: Maximum parsimony recovery conjecture for low-score binary characters
record.statement: Let $T$ be a binary phylogenetic $X$-tree with $|X|=n$. For a character alignment $A_k(T)$ consisting of the binary characters of parsimony score $k$ on $T$, let $k<\frac{n}{4}$. **Maximum parsimony recovery conjecture.** Then $T$ is the unique maximum parsimony tree for $A_k(T)$. This conjecture formalizes the expectation that maximum parsimony uniquely recovers the generating tree when the number of substitutions is sufficiently small; the paper studies this question locally in the NNI neighborhood and motivates the broader recovery claim.
record.source_name: Mareike Fischer, “On the correctness of Maximum Parsimony for data with few substitutions in the NNI neighborhood of phylogenetic trees”, arXiv:2403.01282 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1808.07098](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.07098).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01282

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Global maximum parsimony recovery conjecture for low-score characters
record.statement: Let $T$ be a binary phylogenetic $X$-tree with $|X|=n$. For a character alignment $A_k(T)$ consisting of the binary characters of parsimony score $k$ on $T$, let $k\leq\frac{n-3}{3}$. **Global maximum parsimony recovery conjecture.** Then $T$ is the unique maximum parsimony tree for $A_k(T)$. This is presented as slightly stronger than the preceding conjecture because it asserts unique recovery under a broader bound on $k$; the paper proves a corresponding result within the NNI neighborhood for a smaller range, while global recovery remains open beyond the cases noted in the discussion.

record.title: Wong and Zhu's permanent-index conjecture for the total-weighting matrix
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $A_G$ be the matrix whose rows are indexed by the edges of $G$ and whose columns are indexed by the vertices and edges of $G$, with entries determined by the oriented incidence and adjacency rule described in the source. The **permanent index** of a matrix $A$, denoted by ${\rm pind}(A)$, is the minimum integer $k$ for which there is a matrix formed from columns of $A$, with each column of $A$ used at most $k$ times, and with nonzero permanent.

**Wong and Zhu's conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
{\rm pind}(A_G)=1.
$$

The source relates this permanent-index statement to $(2,2)$-choosability; its resolution is not specified.
record.source_name: T. Wu, J. Luo and Y. Gao, “Some results on total weight choosability”, arXiv:2403.01492 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01492

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Conjecture on the minimum acyclic number of oriented triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $\vec a(n)$ be the minimum of $\vec\alpha(D)$ over all oriented triangle-free graphs $D$ of order $n$, where $\vec\alpha(D)$ denotes the maximum size of an acyclic vertex set. **Minimum acyclic number conjecture.**

$$
\vec a(n)=\Theta\!\left(\sqrt{n\log n}\right).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the triangle-free process and would match the known lower bound up to constant factors, while improving the currently known upper bound asymptotically.
record.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Frédéric Havet, François Pirot and Juliette Schabanel, “Minimum acyclic number and maximum dichromatic number of oriented triangle-free graphs of a given order”, arXiv:2403.02298 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02298

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024). “This conjecture is open even when $H$ is the directed cycle of length $3$.”

record.title: The partial saturation ratio bound for planar graphs of minimum degree at least three
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with minimum degree at least $3$, and write $\operatorname{psr}(G)$ for its partial saturation ratio.

**Planar partial saturation ratio conjecture.** Every such graph satisfies

$$
\operatorname{psr}(G)>\frac{1}{9}.
$$

This is the specialization of the preceding conjecture to $k_1=k_2=0$, identified in the paper as the case of greatest interest. Its status is open in the supplied material.
record.source_name: Alexander Clifton and Nika Salia, “Saturated Partial Embeddings of Planar Graphs”, arXiv:2403.02458 (2024).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02458

record.title: Bermond–Thomassen conjecture on vertex-disjoint cycles
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite simple digraph, and let $f(k)$ be the minimum integer such that every digraph with minimum outdegree at least $f(k)$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles, where $k$ is a positive integer. In view of complete symmetric digraphs, $f(k)\geqslant 2k-1$. **Bermond–Thomassen conjecture.**

$$
f(k)=2k-1.
$$

The conjecture is known for $k=1,2,3$ and remains widely open for $k\geqslant 4$.
record.source_name: Yandong Bai and Wenpei Jia, “Vertex-disjoint cycles of different lengths in tournaments”, arXiv:2403.03692 (2024).
record.references:
**8 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2205.10826](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.10826), [arXiv:1805.02999](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.02999), [arXiv:1708.08641](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08641), [arXiv:1707.02384](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02384), [arXiv:1612.08904](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08904), [arXiv:1610.00876](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.00876), [arXiv:1510.06667](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.06667).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03692

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024). “In view of the complete symmetric digraphs, one can see that $f(k)\geqslant 2k-1$.”

record.title: Ihringer's conjecture on largest $s$-EM-families of $k$-spaces
record.statement: Let an $s$-EM-family of $k$-spaces be a family of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ with matching number at most $s$, and let an intersecting family be one whose members are pairwise non-disjoint. **Ihringer's conjecture.** For $n\geq2k$, if $Y$ is a largest $s$-EM-family of $k$-spaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, then $Y$ is the union of $s$ intersecting families or its complement. The source notes that Ihringer proved this under an additional quantitative condition, but the general conjecture remains unresolved there.
record.source_name: Jiuqiang Liu, Guihai Yu, Lihua Feng and Yongtao Li, “L-intersecting or Configuration Forbidden Families on Set Systems and Vector Spaces over Finite Fields”, arXiv:2403.04289 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04289

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Mubayi's conjecture on d-cluster-free families of subspaces
record.statement:
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $k \ge d \ge 3$ be integers satisfying

$$
n \ge \frac{dk}{d-1}.
$$

For a family $\mathcal{F} \subset \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{V}{k}$, call it **$d$-cluster-free** if it contains no $d$ members whose sum has dimension at most $2k$ and whose intersection is $\{\mathbf{0}_V\}$. **Mubayi's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}$ is $d$-cluster-free, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}| \le \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-1}{k-1}_q,
$$

with equality only if $\mathcal{F}$ is a maximum-sized star. This is the vector-space analogue of the corresponding set-system conjecture; the asserted extremal bound and equality characterization remain open in this generality.
record.source_name: Gabriel Currier and Shahriar Shahriari, “3-cluster-free families of subspaces”, arXiv:2403.04895 (2024).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1903.01622](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01622), [arXiv:1811.07064](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.07064), [arXiv:math/0605171](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605171).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04895

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2024). “For large $n$, the conjecture was settled by Mubayi , Mubayi and Ramadurai and independently F\"{u}redi and \"{O}zkahya .”

record.title: Thomassen's high-girth subgraph conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\delta(G)$ be its minimum degree and let $\operatorname{girth}(G)$ be the length of its shortest cycle, with value $\infty$ when $G$ is acyclic. **Thomassen's conjecture.** There is a function $f:\mathbb{N}^2\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that for any integers $k$ and $d$, every graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\geq f(k,d)$ has a subgraph $H$ satisfying

$$
\delta(H)>d\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{girth}(H)>k.
$$

The conjecture asserts that graphs of simultaneously large minimum degree and girth, known to exist by Erdős's probabilistic construction, occur as subgraphs of every graph with sufficiently large minimum degree. The source reports only partial results, including cases for regular graphs and graphs with controlled maximum degree.
record.source_name: Xiying Du and Rose McCarty, “A survey of degree-boundedness”, arXiv:2403.05737 (2024).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1410.4902](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.4902), [arXiv:1006.0590](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.0590).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05737

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Ribbon-partition conjecture for q-Catalan germs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}=\mathbb{Z}^{a-1}$ be the weight lattice, let $\operatorname{Box}[c'+1,c]$ be the indicated slab of the fundamental box, and order lattice points by the tilted partial order. A ribbon is a saturated chain of length $a$ in this order. **Ribbon-partition conjecture.** If $1\leq c\leq(a-1)^2$, $\gcd(a,c)=1$, and $c'$ is the largest integer less than $c$ satisfying $\gcd(a,c')=1$, then the tilted partial order on

$$
\mathcal{L}\cap\operatorname{Box}[c'+1,c]
$$

has a partition into disjoint ribbons. The conjecture strengthens the standard-partition conjecture and is supported only by small cases $a\in\{3,4,5\}$, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Drew Armstrong, “Lattice Points and Rational q-Catalan Numbers”, arXiv:2403.06318 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.06318

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).
